note: How far each driver's dry evidence goes, layer by layer (DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md item 12.C.1). The ten layers are docs/robot-support.md section 2's: a driver can be wrong at each of them on a machine, and a dry test reaches some and not others. A *suite* is one command that produces evidence: rung (F118: 1 the maker's controller software, 2 the maker's simulator, 3 an independent implementation, 4 a counterpart written in this repository), the exact command, the workflow that runs it (ci.yml on every push, substrates.yml nightly, or null with a `manual` reason), and the layers it reaches. A layer's rung in the matrix is the strongest suite that reaches it. A layer no suite reaches must say why, here or in `defaults`; layers 9 and 10 (the hardware, and the site) are never reached, by any suite, and tools/check-confidence.mjs fails if one claims them. `verified` is the date this row's command was last seen green by whoever wrote it, and is null where nobody has re-run it: the nightly's own record is on the runner, not here. `detection` is the seeded-defect run's result (tools/seed-defects, docs/dry-test-matrix.md), synced from reference/reports/seed-defects.json by `node tools/check-confidence.mjs --sync` and held to it by the check. This file says what evidence exists. It never says a driver works, and no number in it is a probability.

layers.5: the stop and the fault path

defaults.6: the counterpart has no dynamics worth the name: no motors, gains, payload or contact, so nothing here can show a hold that goes limp under load
defaults.7: a simulator's clock is the host's: faults can be injected and refusals checked, but a rate cannot be measured (12.C.5 measures the OS-side budget only, never a robot's latency)
defaults.8: no nightly substrate run covers this driver, so nothing re-measures it when the maker ships a release
defaults.9: no robot: brakes, cables, temperature, wear and encoders that lose count cannot be reached by any dry test
defaults.10: no site: payload and tool configuration, the controller's safety configuration, network setup, calibration and the person at the stop are commissioning, which is human work (§59.6)

chaos.what: the cloud's one HTTP API through a fault-injecting relay: delay, jitter, a slow link, a stall and a blackhole. Found a reply cut off half way raising `IncompleteRead` out of `read_state` and out of a motion (an HTTPException is not an OSError), and a read that waited out the ten seconds a request is given. A read is idempotent and now has two seconds a call and three for the state's two; a request that creates a task keeps its ten, because a timeout does not say the task was not made, and the subject declares the bounds it holds the driver to (a read 3.5 s, a task request 10.5 s: no loop is closed over a cloud). The stop is a local latch and returns at once. The substrate is the fake written here (F15)
